:::{#lem-qf-eigen-bound}
#### A quadratic form is at least the smallest eigenvalue times the squared length

Let $\matr{A}$ be a symmetric $p \times p$ matrix,
and let $\eigval_{\min}$ be the smallest of its [eigenvalues](linear-algebra.qmd#def-eigenvalue).
Then $\tp{\vecf{h}} \matr{A} \vecf{h} \ge \eigval_{\min}\,\norm{\vecf{h}}^2$ for every $\vecf{h} \in \reals^p$.

:::

::: proof

By the [spectral theorem](linear-algebra.qmd#thm-spectral),
write $\matr{A} = \matr{Q} \matr{\Eigvals} \tp{\matr{Q}}$ with $\matr{Q}$ an [orthogonal matrix](linear-algebra.qmd#def-orthogonal-matrix)
and $\matr{\Eigvals} = \diag(\eigval_1, \ldots, \eigval_p)$,
and let $\vecf{y} \eqdef \tp{\matr{Q}} \vecf{h}$.
Then

$$
\ba
\tp{\vecf{h}} \matr{A} \vecf{h}
&= \tp{\vecf{h}} \matr{Q} \matr{\Eigvals} \tp{\matr{Q}} \vecf{h}
&& \text{(substitute the eigendecomposition)}
\\
&= \tp{\vecf{y}} \matr{\Eigvals} \vecf{y}
&& \text{(} \tp{\vecf{h}} \matr{Q} = \tp{(\tp{\matr{Q}} \vecf{h})} \text{, transpose of a product)}
\\
&= \sumip \eigval_i\,y_i^2
&& \text{(} \matr{\Eigvals} \text{ is diagonal)}
\\
&\ge \sumip \eigval_{\min}\,y_i^2
&& \text{(} \eigval_i \ge \eigval_{\min} \text{ and } y_i^2 \ge 0 \text{)}
\\
&= \eigval_{\min}\,\norm{\vecf{y}}^2
&& \text{(the squared length is the sum of squares)}
\\
&= \eigval_{\min}\,\norm{\vecf{h}}^2.
&& \text{(orthogonal matrices preserve length)}
\ea
$$

The second step is the [transpose of a product](linear-algebra.qmd#thm-transpose-product).
The last step applies [orthogonal matrices preserve length](linear-algebra.qmd#thm-orthogonal-norm) to $\tp{\matr{Q}}$.
That theorem applies because $\tp{\matr{Q}}$ is an [orthogonal matrix](linear-algebra.qmd#def-orthogonal-matrix):
since $\matr{Q}$ is [square](linear-algebra.qmd#def-square-matrix) with $\tp{\matr{Q}} \matr{Q} = \matr{I}_p$, also $\matr{Q} \tp{\matr{Q}} = \matr{I}_p$, so

$$
\tp{(\tp{\matr{Q}})} \tp{\matr{Q}} = \matr{Q} \tp{\matr{Q}} = \matr{I}_p.
$$

:::
